minutes.headline: Zoning board continued the Berry solar array hearing to Sept 27 for a stamped plan with dimensions and setbacks
minutes.summary: The board granted a requested extension on a previously granted permit so the applicant could buy an adjoining acre. It then heard a special permit petition for a 23 kW ground-mount solar array on an 8.2 acre lot, where the bylaw asks for 20 acres. Members said the plans lacked dimensions, setbacks and abutter views, so the hearing was continued to September 27 with a stamped plan due a week earlier.

public_comment.topic: Called the system industrial in size and warned an approval would set precedent for the community.

Objected to the array in a rural gateway area. Relayed an outside solar expert's concerns about the code edition, the missing engineer stamp and soil conditions, and worried a variance would set a precedent.

votes.motion: Grant the applicant a two-year extension of the previously granted special permit, though one year was requested.
Motion to continue the Berry hearing, seconded, then a voice vote to close the meeting.

decisions.decision: The permit extension was announced as granted, after a motion to extend it.
The Berry hearing was continued to 7 pm on the 27th, with a stamped plan showing dimensions and setbacks due at least a week before.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals continued the Berry solar array special permit hearing to 7 pm on September 27, asking for a stamped plan with dimensions and setbacks.
Members said the plans lacked dimensions, setbacks and abutter views; the stamped plan is due at least a week before the continued hearing.
The board heard a special permit petition for a ground-mount solar array on a lot smaller than the acreage the bylaw asks for.
The board extended a previously granted special permit for two years, though one year was requested; the vote was not audible in the captions.
Two residents spoke against the array, citing its industrial size, its rural gateway setting, the missing engineer stamp and the precedent an approval could set.

why_it_matters: A solar array on a lot below the bylaw's acreage minimum could set a precedent for how the town treats similar projects on small rural lots, and abutters will want to see the dimensions and setbacks first.
